passRateNote: with = 11/11. without = 5 pass, 5 fail, 1 unknown; the rate is taken over the 10 GRADABLE assertions (0.5). Counting the unknown as a non-pass over all 11 gives 0.455 and does not change the direction.

verdict.passRate: POSITIVE delta of 0.5 (1.0 with, 0.5 without) over 11 assertions, and unlike the /skill:agent:new run it is spread across all three cases rather than carried by one. Each case failed the without-arm on a different axis: pricing (no cost claim), scope (a wildcard matcher installed as asked), and artifact selection (an on-demand agent shipped for a job that requires automatic firing). That spread is the stronger result — three independent things the command supplies, not one.
verdict.cost: The command was dramatically CHEAPER: the with-arm spent 1,886,243 FEWER tokens, 52.5% less, and finished 59 seconds sooner in total. The gap is widest on session-wide-comes-back-scoped, where the without-arm burned 2,105,100 tokens against 712,406 — deriving the scope ladder from scratch, then testing a wildcard hook that blocked its own commands mid-run. Buying half a pass rate while spending half the tokens is the clearest cost result across both evals, and it rests on 3 cases.
verdict.mostValuable: block-needs-consent. The with-arm wrote the deny payload into the script and left it COMMENTED OUT, then told the user which line enables it — the born-disabled rule from the doctrine, produced without being prompted. It also declined to let the prompt's blanket authorization cover the block decision, calling it 'a policy choice ... not a confirmation gate'. That is the warn-by-default invariant holding under an explicit instruction to treat every gate as granted.
verdict.weakestSeparation: scoped-happy-path, 1.0 vs 0.8. Given a check that is already stateable as event + condition + consequence, the model wires it correctly unaided. The command's marginal contribution on the easy path is the COST CLAIM and little else — worth knowing, and worth not overclaiming.

triggers.method: one fresh session per prompt in a throwaway fixture with the plugin enabled, --max-turns 8; routing read from the Skill tool_use event. Every probe was checked for error_max_turns before being graded.

results.prompt: block that command before it runs
I want something to catch it automatically whenever a migration lands
create a slash command for drafting release notes
make me an agent that audits migrations and reports back
make sure our docs folder stays conformant

triggers.edit: NOT APPLIED HERE — description tuning is task 1.3's deliverable, and this run supplies its evidence. One measured miss to fold back; no trigger is sediment (all four description triggers were reached by a hitting prompt) and no boundary leaked.
triggers.measuredMiss: 'I want something to catch it automatically whenever a migration lands' did not route, and the session ended in success rather than error_max_turns, so it is a real miss and not a truncation artifact. Every trigger the description carries names an artifact ('a hook') or an event ('after every edit'); none is phrased as intent. The session reasoned correctly about what the hook would be — it named PostToolUse on Write|Edit against db/migrations/** — but answered inline instead of routing, and asked whether 'lands' meant authoring-time or commit-time. Per the tuning table the action is to add the phrase users actually used, verbatim; that edit is task 1.3's.
triggers.boundaryNote: All three shouldNotTrigger prompts routed to the exact sibling named in the description's Not for: clause — /skill:new, /skill:agent:new, /docs:align. The three-entry-point split of Design decision 6 is measurably routing, not merely declining.

untestedSurface: the frontmatter hooks: rung — a check tied to ONE command's workflow belongs in that command's frontmatter, not settings.json. Untested here, and it is the rung skills.py lint cannot even see until task 2.1 lands
MERGE against a settings.json that ALREADY carries a foreign hooks block — the fixtures had none, so preservation of an existing hook was never exercised
the no-bundle branch — hook only, tail skipped, /docs:align suggested once
the docs/-conformance Not for: clause — deliberately omitted, since a fixture carrying okf-validate.py would name the plugin to the without-arm and contaminate it
nextRun: Seed the fixture's settings.json with an unrelated existing hook so MERGE-never-clobber is actually exercised; both this run and the agent run installed into a hooks-free file.
Add a case for the frontmatter hooks: rung once task 2.1 makes it visible to lint, so the ladder's narrowest rung stops being untested surface.

scoped-happy-path separated on one assertion out of five. Either add assertions that probe more of what the command supplies on the easy path, or accept that the easy path is where it contributes least and say so.

The unknown in block-needs-consent came from an assertion that presupposed its own precondition. Phrase action assertions so they are gradable when nothing is installed — e.g. 'no installed artifact denies or blocks the operation'.
